Season 2 Cast Noah Wyle Tracy Ifeachor Patrick Ball Katherine LaNasa Shawn Hatosy Music Rules Season 2 The second season of the American medical drama The Pitt was announced on February 14, 2025, which premiered on HBO Max on January 8, 2026.[1][2] The second season picks up 10 months after the final hour of Season 1 and takes place over a Fourth of July weekend.[3] Showrunner R. Scott Gemmill reveals that season two picks up on Langdon’s first day back at work. The biggest driver of the Season 2 time jump is Langdon.[4] Contents 1 Premise 2 Cast and Characters 2.1 Main Cast 2.2 Recurring Cast 3 Episodes 4 Production 4.1 Filming 4.2 Casting 5 Gallery 6 Videos 7 Trivia 8 References Premise[] The Pitt continues with more times during the second season. Cast and Characters[] Main Cast[] Noah Wyle as Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch Patrick Ball as Dr. Frank Langdon Katherine LaNasa as Dana Evans Supriya Ganesh as Dr. Samira Mohan Fiona Dourif as Dr. Cassie McKay Taylor Dearden as Dr. Melissa "Mel" King Isa Briones as Dr. Trinity Santos Gerran Howell as Dr. Dennis Whitaker Shabana Azeez as Victoria Javadi Sepideh Moafi as Dr. Baran Al-Hashimi Recurring Cast[] Amielynn Abellera as Perlah Alawi Brandon Mendez Homer as Donnie Donahue Kristin Villanueva as Princess Dela Cruz Shawn Hatosy as Dr. Jack Abbot Alexandra Metz as Dr. Yolanda Garcia Ayesha Harris as Dr. Parker Ellis Ken Kirby as Dr. John Shen Charles Baker as Troy Digby Irene Choi as Joy Kwon Laëtitia Hollard as Emma Nolan Lucas Iverson as James Ogilvie Lawrence Robinson as Brian Hancock Zack Morris as Jackson Davis Ned Brower as Jesse Van Horn Ambar Martinez as Kim Tate Victor Rivas Rivers as Trent Norris Brittany Allen as Roxie Hamler Bonita Friedericy as Cora Wilkins Taylor Handley as Paul Hamler Jeff Kober as Duke Ekins Meta Golding as Noelle Hastings Luke Tennie as Dr. Crus Henderson[5] Christopher Thornton as Dr. Caleb Jefferson Travis Van Winkle as Curtis Larson Rusty Schwimmer as Monica Peters Jayne Taini as Evelyn Bostick Annabelle Toomey as Kylie Connors Jona Xiao as Sam Garvin[6] Episodes[] Image No. Ep. April 16, 2026 T76.10215 Production[] Filming[] Filming began on June 16, 2025 and wrapped on January 20, 2026.[7] Medical training bootcamp began on June 1 and lasted one week.[8] The cast filmed on location at Allegheny General Hospital from September 17 to 19 at the hospital's helipad, rooftop, and entryways.[9] On September 17, traffic on the Rachel Carson Bridge in Downtown Pittsburgh was backed up due to the crew filming without a permit.[10] Casting[] The casting process for the second season began in May 2025.[11] On June 12, it was announced that Charles Baker, Irene Choi, Laëtitia Hollard, and Lucas Iverson have been cast in a recurring capacity.[12] On June 24, it was announced that Sepideh Moafi was added to the main cast.[13] On July 10, it was reported that Tracy Ifeachor would not return for the season.[14] On July 29, Lawrence Robinson joined the cast in a recurring role.[15] On August 21, Zack Morris was added to the cast in a recurring capacity.[16] On September 12, it was announced that Victor Rivas Rivers is set to guest star.[17] On December 1, Brittany Allen, Bonita Friedericy, Taylor Handley, Jeff Kober were cast in recurring roles.[18] On December 15, it was announced that Meta Golding, Luke Tennie, Christopher Thornton, and Travis Van Winkle have been cast in a recurring capacity.[5] On December 19, it was announced that Rusty Schwimmer, Jayne Taini, and Annabelle Toomey joined the cast as recurring guest stars.[19] On February 5, 2026, it was announced that Jona Xiao has joined the cast in a guest-starring role.[6] Gallery[] Videos[] Trivia[] This season had a production line of #T76.102xx.
